//: Palette-swap variants for the Godot renderer (SP-8).
A sprite drawn through a palette is treated as a grayscale master: the
shader takes each texel's luminance and looks it up in a colour ramp. So a
creature that differs from another only in colour needs no sprite of its
own -- it needs a redirect and six hex values.
That is not a hypothetical saving. UltimateCataclysm ships art for 134 of
the game's 195 zombie types, and a large share of the missing 61 are the
'dusted' and 'fungalize' families: the same creature, coated in fungal
spores. Before this they fell through the sprite chain to a generic
placeholder. Now they draw the creature they actually are, in the colour
the infection would make it.
Fields:
palettes[].id    referenced by variants[].palette
palettes[].ramp  dark to light; sampled as a 1-D ramp, so entries are
interpolated and three is coarse where eight is smooth
variants[].id      the tileset id being defined
variants[].sprite  draw this id's sprite instead (optional)
variants[].palette recolour through this palette (optional)
A tileset may override this wholesale with its own godot_palettes.json in
its gfx directory; see godot_tileset_loader::load_palettes.
This file is not game data. It sits beside data/shaders/ rather than under
data/json/, so the JSON loader never walks it and it needs no 'type'.

palettes.//: Dusted: coated in dry spores. Chalky, desaturated, slightly warm.
Fungalizing: the bloom has taken hold. Grey-green, cold, damp.
Irradiated: sickly yellow-green with a hot highlight.
